description.value: The study examined whether simple multiplication processing differs between the language in which bilingual adults learned multiplication and their other language, using behavioral and fMRI measures.

spans.text: Critically, L1 was not always equivalent to the language of learning multiplication (LA+).

design.value: Within-subject bilingual fMRI study using English and Spanish multiplication verification, verbal and numerosity localizers, ROI analyses, exploratory whole-brain analyses, hierarchical regressions, and Bayesian modeling.

spans.text: Participants performed two localizer tasks (verbal and numerosity) and the experimental task (single-digit multiplication verification) in a single experimental session.

2.3.1 Single-digit multiplication verification task

task_description.value: Participants heard two spoken number words, followed by a visual Arabic digit, and determined whether the Arabic digit was the correct product.

spans.text: For this task, participants heard two spoken number words, followed by a visual Arabic digit, and the task was to determine whether the Arabic digit was the correct product of the two spoken numbers (i.e., determine if the problem was true or false).
Event-related statistical analysis was performed according to the general linear model (GLM).

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to determine whether the Arabic digit was the correct product and respond with their index finger for true and middle finger for false.

spans.text: Participants used their index finger if the proposed solution was true and their middle finger if the proposed solution was false.

stimuli.value: spoken English or Spanish number words and a visual Arabic digit
